messages:
Maria: Quick heads-up — the rollout for the new routing policy hit a guard and traffic to variant B was throttled down automatically at 14:21. Do we stop the experiment or collect more?
Samir: I noticed that too. Console shows a sample-ratio mismatch: B has ~0.78x the expected exposures. Suspect missing instrumentation + a shard issue.
Noah: Root cause looks like edge warmup pings from older SDKs not setting `route_id`. I opened PR #4321 to add `route_id` for warmup and small clients.
deploy-bot: Canary guard triggered: `latency_p95 > 250ms` for route `chat-gen` on variant B — auto-scaling adjusted and assignment reduced to 5% at 14:22.
Maria: That timing is unfortunate — guard reduced traffic exactly when B needed samples. Stopping now could bias the effect estimate upward.
Julie: Agreed. We should run a quick post-hoc power estimate + bias check before deciding. I can run telemetry queries.
Samir: Also we should debate assignment policy: do we temporarily bump B to collect enough N, or reroute new sessions deterministically to limit churn?
Noah: Deterministic hashing for new sessions is a config flip (low risk). But if route_id is missing we still can't attribute exposures to cohort reliably.
Maria: Action items: Julie — compute conditional power and bias; Noah — push patch to set `route_id` on warmup pings; Samir — add a lightweight analytic comparing expected vs observed by stratum. Decision target: EOD.
Julie: Running numbers now. Current counts: N_A=12,432, N_B=1,054. Observed lift (CTR) = +3.4%. Two-sided p ≈ 0.043. With balanced 50/50 we'd need ~20k per arm for 80% power at a 2% lift.
Samir: So with current skew we won't hit power. Options: (1) increase B to ~20% for a short pulse to harvest samples, (2) keep conservative allocation and run longer, (3) post-stratify by session type if missingness is ignorable.
Noah: Increasing B risks exposing more customers to a faulty variant (latency). Maybe do a short, monitored pulse with circuit breaker.
Maria: We also need the console UX to show assignment drift/instrumentation-missing flags. Right now we only surface stat-sig and latency cards, which misses this class of problem.
Julie: I'll add a dashboard widget: expected vs observed exposures per cohort and a warning if `route_id` missing > 1%. Also a small power meter that shows time-to-power given current allocation.
deploy-bot: Patch candidate deployed to edge: `edge/v2.3.1-rc` — warmup pings now set `route_id`.
Samir: Added quick SQL to analytics repo to compute drift:
```
select cohort,
       count(*) as observed,
       sum(expected_prob) as expected
from exposures
where ts between '2025-11-06' and '2025-11-06 23:59'
group by cohort;
```
Noah: After the patch rolls, run that and check if observed_B >= 8k. If not, we should either pause or do a small pulse to 20% for 2 hours under strict monitors.
Maria: Sounds good. Quick sync in 30 to review numbers. Please drop findings to this thread. :clock1: :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
Julie: Will do. Initial bias check: if missingness correlates with device type we'll need to reweight, not just recluster. I'll flag that in my run.
Samir: FYI I've added a guard to the rollout service to emit a `assignment_drift` metric when |observed-expected|/expected > 0.05 per stratum.
Noah: Nice. That will help ops surface problems earlier.
Maria: Thanks everyone. If patch proves clean, we can consider a short lift plus a canary guard change that ignores artifacts from warmup pings.
analysis-bot: Telemetry job `exposure-compare` finished — current missing `route_id` rate: 2.3% (higher on older clients).
Julie: That's actionable. Noah, please prioritize the patch rolling to prod. I'll re-run power calc once deploy-bot confirms rollout.
deploy-bot: Rollout to prod edge fleet started (canary 1/5). Monitor `latency_p95` and `assignment_drift`.
Maria: Copy — keeping thread open.
